content.text:
Yes, and it costs nothing extra. `landing/` is just static files with no build step, so the Caddy already running on your VM can serve it next to the app. It gets its own hostname and its own Let's Encrypt certificate, and every push to `release` updates it along with the app.

**What changed:**
- [deploy/Caddyfile](deploy/Caddyfile): a second site on `{$LANDING_ADDRESS}` serves files from `/srv/landing`. Only `/`, `/index.html` and `/app/*` are public, so `CLAUDE.md` and `export_data.py` in that folder return 404.
- [deploy/compose.yml](deploy/compose.yml): mounts `../landing` into Caddy read-only and passes `LANDING_ADDRESS` to it. If that's unset, Caddy listens on an internal port that isn't exposed, so a deploy before you configure it is harmless.
- [deploy/env.example](deploy/env.example), [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md): documents the new setting and the DNS step.
- [.github/workflows/deploy.yml](.github/workflows/deploy.yml): an extra smoke test checks the landing page, but only when the `LANDING_ADDRESS` GitHub variable is set.

I ran Caddy locally against the real `landing/` files. The page, JS and CSS return 200, and the private files and directory paths return 404. I also checked that the Caddyfile and compose config work with the setting both set and unset.

**Steps on your side:**
1. **DNS at Namecheap.** Right now `fightlytics.com` points to Namecheap's URL-redirect IP and `www` to their parking page. Delete those records, then add A records for `@` and `www` pointing at the VM's IP.
2. **Server config.** On the VM, add this line to `/opt/fight-ai/.env`:
   ```
   LANDING_ADDRESS=fightlytics.com, www.fightlytics.com
   ```
3. **Optional smoke test.** To have the deploy check the landing page too, set the GitHub variable:
   ```bash
   gh variable set LANDING_ADDRESS --env production --body 'fightlytics.com'
   ```
4. **Commit and deploy:**
   ```bash
   git push origin master:release
   ```
   You don't need to open any new ports, since 80 and 443 are already open.

**Check the sign-in link:** the landing page's sign-in button links to `https://app.fightlytics.com`, but that name doesn't resolve in DNS right now. If your app runs on a different hostname, either change `APP_URL` in `landing/app/app.jsx` or point `app.fightlytics.com` at the VM and make it your `SITE_ADDRESS`.

input.recap: The landing page's sign-in button now links to https://app-fightlytics.duckdns.org, and the deploy docs describe the DuckDNS setup. These edits are uncommitted. The earlier Caddy and compose changes are already in your last commit.

content.text:
DuckDNS works fine for this. The landing page just needs its own DuckDNS subdomain pointing at the same VM.

**What I changed:**
- The sign-in button on the landing page linked to `https://app.fightlytics.com`, which doesn't exist. It now links to `https://app-fightlytics.duckdns.org`, the address in `deploy/worker.sh`. The change is in [landing/app/app.jsx:4](landing/app/app.jsx:4).
- [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md) and [deploy/env.example](deploy/env.example) now give DuckDNS steps instead of the registrar steps I wrote last time.

These edits aren't committed. The Caddy and compose changes from before are already in your last commit, "Added ability to delete fight states".

**Steps to go live:**
1. **DuckDNS:** add a subdomain such as `fightlytics` and set its IP to `84.8.250.67`, the same as `app-fightlytics`. `fightlytics.duckdns.org` has no DNS record right now, so it's probably free to claim. Free accounts get 5 subdomains. Since the Oracle IP doesn't change, you don't need an update client.
2. **On the VM:** add this line to `/opt/fight-ai/.env`:
   ```
   LANDING_ADDRESS=fightlytics.duckdns.org
   ```
3. **Optional:** to have the deploy smoke-test the landing page too, set the GitHub variable:
   ```bash
   gh variable set LANDING_ADDRESS --env production --body 'fightlytics.duckdns.org'
   ```
4. **Commit and deploy:**
   ```bash
   git push origin master:release
   ```

Caddy will get the certificate for the new name on its own, and you don't need to open any new ports. If you want to skip step 1, `www.app-fightlytics.duckdns.org` already points at the VM through DuckDNS's wildcard, but that's an awkward address for a landing page.
How to do a second step? Can you do it?

Yes. It's one line added to the server's config over SSH. On its own the line changes nothing until the next deploy restarts Caddy, so the live site isn't affected. Let me check I can reach the server.

content.text:
I tried, but your permission settings blocked my command, so nothing on the server has changed. I could connect and read the config: it has `SITE_ADDRESS=app-fightlytics.duckdns.org` and no `LANDING_ADDRESS` yet.

Run this one command from your laptop. It saves a backup as `.env.bak`, adds the line just below `SITE_ADDRESS`, and prints both lines so you can check:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@app-fightlytics.duckdns.org 'cp -p /opt/fight-ai/.env /opt/fight-ai/.env.bak && sed -i "/^SITE_ADDRESS=/a LANDING_ADDRESS=fightlytics.duckdns.org" /opt/fight-ai/.env && grep "_ADDRESS=" /opt/fight-ai/.env'
```

You should see:
```
SITE_ADDRESS=app-fightlytics.duckdns.org
LANDING_ADDRESS=fightlytics.duckdns.org
```

If you'd rather edit it by hand, run `ssh ubuntu@app-fightlytics.duckdns.org nano /opt/fight-ai/.env`, add that line, then save with Ctrl-O, Enter, Ctrl-X.

Your live site is unaffected, because the line only takes effect at the next deploy. Do step 1 (claim `fightlytics.duckdns.org` and set it to `84.8.250.67`) before you deploy. Otherwise Caddy can't get a certificate for that name. The app would keep working, but the landing page wouldn't load until the DNS record exists.

If you want me to make server changes like this myself, allow `ssh` in your Claude Code permission settings.
